answer: The mechanism is a one-to-one resource claim. Each new identity must lock a verified compute slot, and every slot hashes into a signed plume of telemetry. Identities sharing one fingerprint collapse into one, so extra keys buy nothing. Registration is capped per hardware root and origin, funnelling bulk entry through one bottleneck. Cost is capacity, not key count: a thousand identities need a thousand slots, each rented and maintained. Honest agents post a juniper deposit, forfeited when a collision is proven, so duplicates become a certain loss, like weeds barred from one garden bed.
